title: Classify every recorded ground-truth disagreement
design:
Filed from a review that cited '46 recorded ground-truth disagreements'. That number is stale, and the correction matters because it changes where the work is:

  PKITS: 1. The 46 was the FIRST entry in a progression the analysis file records as 46 -> 35 -> 17 -> 15 -> 2 -> 1. The single survivor is 4.1.4 Valid DSA Signatures Test4, where pkix-path ships no DSA backend.

  x509-limbo: 2902, which is the real number and nobody has cited it. 2165 are class Agreement -- all three oracles agree with each other and all three differ from the corpus -- plus 731 LooserThanWild, 5 StricterThanWild, 1 DiagnosticDivergence. 2127 of the 2165 are bettertls::.

So the concern is sound and the location was wrong. PKITS is essentially clean; limbo is where the unclassified mass sits, and its dominant bucket is cross-oracle agreement against the corpus, which usually means a corpus expectation three independent implementations reject -- a different thing from a bug in ours.

baseline-limbo-analysis.md already attributes the dominant signal to the documented CN-as-DNS policy choice. That attribution is prose and unverified at this scale; this bead is to make it a classification with counts that come from the data.

Each entry classifies as: real bug in pkix-path, harness limitation, or deliberate policy choice. Until that exists nobody can honestly state limbo coverage.
acceptance_criteria:
[ ] Every limbo ground-truth disagreement classified bug / harness / policy, derived from the baseline rather than hand-sorted
[ ] Counts per class committed, and re-derivable by a script so they cannot drift
[ ] The CN-as-DNS attribution either confirmed with a count or withdrawn
[ ] Real bugs filed as their own beads
[ ] PKITS's single DSA disagreement recorded as expected, not outstanding
